input.quote: c. the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
input.rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose mirror-image caps on IBM and on Customer at the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid in the preceding 12 months, so the cap is mutual and 12-month-fees based, indemnification payments sit outside that cap as a separate liability item (9.1(a)/9.2(a)), and Section 10 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually. However, the caps contain no carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and Section 6 expressly makes Sections 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment, so confidentiality breaches are capped. That fails the fallback checklist on a material term. We propose one short mutual carve-out sentence at the fallback level rather than upgrading the cap formula; the $100,000 floor (versus our preferred USD 1,000,000) and the absence of data-protection and IP-infringement carve-outs are noted but not pressed here.

ops.text: The limitations in Subsections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) do not apply to either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence, or wilful misconduct.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We add a short mutual carve-out so that a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and wilful misconduct sit outside the Section 9 caps; our fallback position requires those carve-outs alongside indemnification. The mutual greater-of $100,000 / 12-months-of-charges cap and the uncapped indemnification payments are otherwise unchanged.
proposal.summary: Add mutual carve-out from the Section 9 caps for confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
